main_text.p: quas efferre poterant, virtutis ergò victore liber abitus permissus. His nova sedes Melita insula à Carolo v Imper. data, quam etiam nunc fortiter tuentur.
main_text.head: XII. DE REPVBLICA ET FORTVNA ACHÆORVM.
main_text.p: CHAIA, quæ proprie sic di-cta, à finibus Sicyonis secundum Corinthiacum ad fretum angustum, & inde porrò secundum Ionium mare ad initium Elidis porrigitur. Ea ut incolas quondam varios habuit, ita varia nomina accepit. Antiquissimis temporibus ipsa Ægialea, & habitatores Ægialenses dicti fuêre. Deinde ab Ionibus ex Attica profectis, quibus appellationem dederat Ion Xuthi filius, Hellenis nepos, Deucalionis Thessali pronepos, Erechthei Athenienfium regis filia Creusa natus, occupata & infesta, Ioniæ nomen tulit, in partes xii divisa. Iones demum ab Achæis agnatis suis Laconicâ ab Heraclidis Eurysthene & Procle ejectis, duce Tisameno Orestis filio iftinc expulsi in Atticam redierunt: dehinc post com-plurium[illegible, ~12 letters]

page.notes: The bottom-left margin holds small, badly damaged marginal marks (fragments such as "Occ", "c : cp", "t : db : Jic", "occ"). I could not read them reliably, so I have left them out of the transcription. The note element above is a placeholder for them. The scan is faint at the right edge, and I read the long s as plain s throughout. The line "dehinc post com-" is continued by "plurium" at the line end, which gives "complurium". The word "fuêre" is printed with a circumflex. The lowercase "v" in "Carolo v Imper." is kept as printed.
